name: SkiErg Double-Pole Pull
description: The SkiErg simulates the double-pole motion of cross-country skiing, pulling two handles downward from an overhead position with a simultaneous hip hinge, engaging the latissimus dorsi, core, triceps, and deltoids under a continuous cardiovascular load. Each stroke begins with the arms raised overhead and ends with a powerful downward pull and hip extension, creating a cyclical full-body pulling pattern. The SkiErg develops both upper-body strength-endurance and cardiovascular conditioning while remaining completely non-impact.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing the SkiErg machine with feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp both handles with arms extended overhead, body tall, slight forward lean at the hips.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the damper (resistance) to 4–6. Plug in the performance monitor and select meters or time for the interval target.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended overhead and a slight hip hinge. This is the catch position.
Step 2: Simultaneously pull both handles downward and hinge the hips forward, bringing the handles past the hips to the finish position.
Step 3: At the finish, the handles are near the hips, body is hinged forward with a flat back, and the core is fully contracted.
Step 4: Recover by allowing the arms to rise overhead as the hips extend back to the start position in a smooth, continuous motion.
Step 5: Maintain a consistent stroke rate — typically 30–40 strokes per minute for intervals.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply on the downward pull (the drive phase). Inhale on the recovery as the arms rise back overhead.
common_mistakes: Pulling only with the arms without engaging the hip hinge, which loses the core and hip contribution
Letting the elbows bend excessively rather than keeping a long lever during the pull
Letting go of a smooth rhythm and jerking the handles
safety_considerations: Avoid rounding the lower back at the bottom of the pull — maintain a neutral spine throughout the hip hinge
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arms travel from fully overhead to past the hips. The hip hinge should be pronounced — torso moves from tall to roughly 45° forward.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Interval: 500m hard / 2 minutes rest × 5. Time-based: 30 seconds hard / 30 seconds rest × 10. Stroke rate: 30–40 SPM during hard effort.
coaching_cues: Lead with the hip hinge, not just the arms
Think of pulling the handles through the floor
Keep long arms — do not bend the elbows early
